newsitem.title: BULGARIA: Bulgaria lets market set prices of bad debt bonds.
newsitem.headline: Bulgaria lets market set prices of bad debt bonds.

text.p: Bulgaria's government scrapped on Monday minimum prices for domestic bad debt bonds, known as ZUNKs, as part of preparations to launch an IMF-prescribed currency board system, the cabinet press centre said.

"Abolishing minimum prices for ZUNKs is part of the memorandum of financial policies agreed with the IMF and will boost trade in the bonds on the secondary market," a press centre official told reporters.
Under a $657 million reform and funding agreement with the IMF, Bulgaria is to introduce a fixed-exchange rate mechanism, called a currency board, from July 1 to stabilise the economy.
Under the currency board system, the lev will be pegged to the mark and foreign exchange reserves mast match levs in circulation.

The official said minimum prices were no longer necessary because increased investor interest had raised market prices after the proportion of bonds permitted in payment for privatisations was increased.

Local banks now trade dollar-denominated ZUNKs at 60-63 percent of par, much higher than their minimum acceptable price of 45 percen. Lev-denominated bonds traded at 61-62.5 percent of par compared to a minimum acceptable price of 35 percent.

In April, the interim cabinet allowed payment in ZUNKs for up to 80 percent of the price of privatised medium- and small-state enterprises, up from a previous 50 percent. The bonds are accepted as a means of payment at par value in sell-offs.
The 50-percent limit remained in force for big enterprises to be privatised this year. Bulgaria expects $300-350 million from the sale of those firms.
Bad debt bonds worth 32 billion levs and $1.8 billion, respectively, were issued three years ago to cover banks' non-performing loans extended to state companies before 1991.
There were $917.6 million and 19.8 billion levs ($11.7 million) worth of ZUNK bonds in circulation by June 9, central bank figures showed.

High yields, pending sell-offs, and expectations of low exchange rate risk under the currency board system have attracted some $130 million investment in government securities from foreign investors in the past several months. -- Sofia Newsroom +359-2 911 88 ($ = 1698 Bulgarian Levs)
